questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Troubleshooting and Recovery”?
options: Troubleshooting and Recovery should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Troubleshooting and Recovery helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Troubleshooting and Recovery means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Troubleshooting and Recovery removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
questions.answer_key: Troubleshooting and Recovery helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Troubleshooting and Recovery is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Resolving dependency conflicts” in this lesson?
options: Connect “Resolving dependency conflicts” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Resolving dependency conflicts” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Resolving dependency conflicts” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Resolving dependency conflicts” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Resolving dependency conflicts” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Resolving dependency conflicts” under Troubleshooting and Recovery. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Troubleshooting and Recovery”?
options: Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
